title: Train Smarter, Not Harder: Switching Signal-Guided Training in Active Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.06806v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Training strategy, namely whether to retrain from scratch or fine-tune from the previous checkpoint, is an overlooked decision variable in active learning. We show that this choice has exploitable structure: retraining is most useful in early rounds, when each batch can substantially reshape the labeled distribution, while fine-tuning becomes safer once the model trajectory stabilizes. We propose HybridAL, an adaptive training schedule that monitors an online stabilization signal and switches from retraining to fine-tuning after sustained stabilization. translated_title: 更聪明地训练，而非更努力地训练：主动学习中的切换信号引导训练
translated_abstract: 训练策略，即是从头重新训练还是从上一个检查点进行微调，是主动学习中一个被忽视的决策变量。我们证明这一选择具有可利用的结构特征：重新训练在早期轮次中最有用，此时每个批次都能显著重塑已标注数据的分布；而一旦模型轨迹趋于稳定，微调就变得更安全。我们提出HybridAL，一种自适应训练调度方法，它监控在线稳定化信号，并在持续稳定后从重新训练切换到微调。两个互补的信号——谱指数变化Δα（基于权重）和准确率变化ΔAcc（基于验证集）——在时间-校准权衡上覆盖不同的位置。在三个编码器骨干网络和六个文本分类任务（每个任务五个随机种子）上，HybridAL保持端点macro-F1不劣于重新训练和微调（边际为0.010），并节省了高达49%的重训练开销
tldr: 提出HybridAL自适应训练调度方法，通过监控在线稳定化信号在主动学习中智能地从重新训练切换到微调，在保持性能不劣化的同时节省高达49%的重训练开销
en_tdlr: HybridAL is an adaptive training schedule for active learning that monitors online stabilization signals to intelligently switch from retraining to fine-tuning, saving up to 49% of retraining costs while maintaining non-inferior performance
